comments.body: 2026-11-07: the owner settled the question this card asked. Yes, opt-out if not too complex, and encryption only if it cannot cost reliability, which rules out application-level encryption. Rewritten as a feature and moved out of uncommitted.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Decided by the owner on 2026-11-07: yes, on by default with an opt-out, and it has to just work. A restored pane comes back with its history above a new shell, where today the restart notice says "the scrollback is gone".

**Storage: plain files, mode 0600, beside the daemon's other state.** persist.rs already writes that way, through a temporary file and a rename. Application-level encryption is left out on purpose. A daemon starts with nobody at the keyboard, through launchd or over SSH, so it must read its key unprompted. A key on the same disk protects nothing, the Keychain can prompt or refuse, and a Linux devenv has no equivalent. Each failure there would lose history, which is the reliability the owner ruled out risking. FileVault or the disk's own encryption covers a machine at rest, and any program running as the same user can already read a pane through `muster pane read`.

**What to write: the primary screen's history and text, not the whole replay.** The process that drew the screen is gone, so a restored pane must not inherit an alternate screen, mouse modes, keyboard modes or a kitty stack, and it must not carry a replay continuation (a_2vgzfWBEl): an unfinished sequence would swallow the new shell's first output. The primary-screen formatter from patch 0001 is the likely source. Keep VT text, not a libghostty snapshot: any later libghostty can read it, while snapshot/main.zig calls its format version 1 "the work-in-progress format that we intended to continue to break", and readers check only that number, so an old file could decode into a subtly wrong grid. Snapshots would also lose saved history at every re-pin.

**It must never get in a restore's way.** A missing, short or unreadable file means the pane starts empty and a warning goes to the log. A restore does not wait on it. Delete a pane's file when the pane closes, including when reopening it is no longer possible.

**Open, for the plan:**
- When to save. There is no incremental encode, so each save formats a whole pane under its lock, and a crash loses what came after the last save. Saving an idle pane that changed, plus at a clean shutdown, is the obvious start. Measure the hold at 50 MB: `vt.replay_compose` is 235 ns a row, and input waits on that lock.
- Handover needs none of this, since the panes live on.
- Disk use: up to about 750 MB at 15 full panes at the 50 MB default, or less if a file is compressed.
- Time Machine and other backups copy home directories, so a file of terminal contents should be excluded, and on work machines it must stay out of personal backups. An `tmutil addexclusion` on the directory may be enough on a Mac.
- The setting's name and place, likely a root key such as `persist_scrollback = false`, following CLAUDE.md's "Configuring".

**Docs this changes.** docs/architecture.md's "Persist intent, never observation" needs a stated exception with this reason: a person would ask for their history again, even though its contents are observed. CLAUDE.md's "Sessions outlive the app" desideratum and the notice in crates/muster-core/src/mirror/restart.rs both say the scrollback is lost.

A persisted format is design work and a risky change: get the plan reviewed by the other model family before building, and two reviewers on the result (ordo `design-work`, `push`).
title: A pane's scrollback survives a daemon restart, with an opt-out
